title: Commit watermarks and canonicalization for sideband & compressed stream metering
creator: Asha Patel
description: Edge cases in streaming metering that lead to persistent over- or under-charging when sideband messages (function/tool outputs, system events) and compressed/opaque attachments change tokenization after transport. This ticket adds deterministic commit watermarks, canonicalization rules for compressed attachments, and a provisional+final crediting model to ensure credits are correct even when frames are retransmitted, decompressed server-side, or delivered out-of-order.
background: Recent incidents reported by finance and customer success show customers being billed for attachment bytes that are later dropped during pipeline decompression or for speculative function outputs that were aborted mid-stream. Existing heuristics provisionally credit tokens on receipt-of-chunk which makes accounting fragile for compressed blobs and sideband frames that are transformed by the runtime. We need a low-latency approach that avoids long-tail charge adjustments but guarantees eventual correctness and auditability.
investigation_findings: Observed cases where client sent compressed attachment (gzip) chunked across WS frames; server concatenation+decompression changed token boundaries -> reported token_count mismatch vs final parsed payload.

Sideband frames (system messages and function outputs) are currently metered using frame-length heuristics; speculative partial outputs that are later aborted have provisional credits that are hard to reconcile without finalization markers.
Rate-limiter backpressure and proxy retries cause duplicate/partial frame deliveries that created transient double-crediting in 2% of fuzzed sessions in our test harness.
Current ledger entries lack a stable content checksum and finalization flag, which complicates retroactive corrections and audits.
Billing pipeline downstream (billing-aggregator) cannot reliably defer charging without exposing customers to unbounded provisional debt or excessive latency in quota enforcement.
proposal_summary: Introduce a commit-watermark event emitted by the serving runtime for each session or logical request describing: canonicalized token_count, CRC32 checksum of canonicalized input and sideband payloads, finalization timestamp, and a deterministic 'finalization reason' (completed|aborted|switched-model). Metering pipeline will: (1) accept provisional credits at chunk receipt but mark them provisional, (2) apply final adjustments on receipt of commit-watermark, and (3) persist both provisional and final ledger entries with provenance links. For compressed attachments, add canonicalization rules (decompress then normalize whitespace and unicode NFKC before tokenizing) so transient transport encodings do not change token counts.
implementation_steps: Runtime: Add commit-watermark API on session termination and model-switch boundaries (protobuf schema + WS control frame).
Runtime: Emit CRC32 and canonicalization metadata (encoding, decompressed size, token_count_hint).
Metering pipeline: Flag provisional credits on initial chunk events. Store provisional ledger rows with session_id + sequence_number + provisional=true.
Metering pipeline: On commit-watermark, compute canonical token_count via canonicalizer and reconcile provisional rows -> emit correction rows (delta credits) if needed.
Canonicalizer library: Implement decompress-then-normalize tokenization path for gzip/deflate and common content-types (text/plain, application/json, application/octet-stream fallback).

Backward compatibility: If runtime does not emit commit-watermark within X seconds, run conservative finalization heuristic and mark finalization_reason=timed_out (small reconciler job to avoid indefinite provisional charges).
Testing: Extend fuzz harness to simulate compressed chunk splits, proxy retries, and mid-stream model handoffs; assert ledger invariants (sum(provisional)+sum(corrections) == canonical token_count).
Monitoring: Dashboard with provisional vs finalized delta counts, rate of commit-watermarks missing per region, and top sessions with frequent corrections.
Docs & Support: Update billing FAQ and API docs to describe provisional credits and expected reconciliation window.
acceptance_criteria: Canonicalizer library implements gzip/deflate decompression + unicode NFKC + whitespace normalization and has unit tests with edge-case inputs (emoji sequences, surrogate pairs, CRLF combos).
Runtime emits commit-watermark for >95% of sessions in staging; missing-watermark rate reduced to <0.2% after rollout; metric tracked in dashboard.
End-to-end test harness demonstrates determinism: simulated fragmented compressed upload -> ledger finalization matches direct canonical token_count for 1000 randomized fuzz inputs.
Billing-aggregator receives correction rows and final customer invoices/net charges equal to canonical token counts (no unexplained >0.5% variance in test tenant).
No customer-visible quota regressions in canary (dedicated region); provisional credits do not allow customers to exceed hard-quotas beyond allowed grace window.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Increased tail latency if we wait for commit-watermarks before final charging. Mitigation: provisional credits remain to enable low-latency behavior; finalization adjusts within configurable window.

Risk: Canonicalization might disagree with client-side tokenizers for edge Unicode cases. Mitigation: publish canonicalizer rules and provide SDK tokenizers that mirror server behavior; add opt-in client-side verification hooks.
Risk: Storage overhead of provisional+correction ledger rows. Mitigation: compact old finalized entries weekly into a single anchored row and archive raw provisional rows after retention window.

Risk: Rollout complexity across runtime versions. Mitigation: design commit-watermark as optional control frame; older runtimes will fall back to conservative heuristics (timed_out finalization) and be migrated gradually.
monitoring_and_rollout: Canary in staging region (eu-west-1) 10% traffic -> observe provisional_delta_ratio metric.
If provisional_delta_ratio < 0.01 and missing-watermark < 0.2%, expand to 50% then 100% over 3 days.
Alert if reconciliation corrections exceed 0.5% of token volume for >30m or if missing-watermark spikes above 1%.
Create Grafana dashboard panels: provisional_tokens, finalized_tokens, correction_delta, missing_watermark_rate, top-reconciled-sessions.
Support plan: experiment runbook for refunds, customer notifications, and how to opt-out during migration windows.
